extracted.intended_audience: Authors, referees, and editors involved with submissions to Life Science Alliance (LSA)
extracted.subtask_description: Journal editorial and peer‑review policies governing submission assessment, peer review, revisions, appeals, transfers, transparency, and scooping protection for manuscripts submitted to Life Science Alliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial editorial assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions are initially assessed by a dedicated scientific editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This primary screening determines whether manuscripts proceed to peer review. It is the first gate in the editorial workflow; no further scoring guidance provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review for research manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: All research manuscripts published in Life Science Alliance are subject to peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research manuscripts judged potentially suitable for publication with realistic experimental revision are sent out for formal peer review, typically to three appropriate independent experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability criterion: realistic experimental revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts are sent for formal peer review if judged by the editors to be potentially suitable for publication in Life Science Alliance with realistic experimental revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors assess whether requested experimental work and revisions are realistic within one major round; only manuscripts with a high probability of acceptance after one major round are invited for revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number and independence of referees
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts are typically reviewed by three appropriate independent experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may exclude a small number of experts if they are concerned of a conflict of interest or bias. Editors select referees considered appropriate and independent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict-of-interest / exclusion of reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may exclude a small number of experts if they are concerned of a conflict of interest or bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusions should be justified by authors at submission; editors retain discretion over reviewer selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary evaluation standard: strength of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts are critically evaluated for strong evidence to support the conclusions that are drawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and referees should focus on whether the data and analyses robustly support conclusions. The evaluation explicitly excludes consideration of perceived impact, author or institution prestige, and likely citation metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of impact/prestige/metrics bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither the perceived impact nor the prestige of the authors or their institutions is taken into account in the evaluation of manuscripts. The likelihood an article will be cited or contribute to other journal metrics is also not considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions should be evidence‑based and independent of author/institution reputation or citation potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referee cross‑commenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees are routinely invited to comment on each other’s reports and may discuss issues under moderation of the editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees are not informed of each other’s identities. Cross‑commenting is used to clarify disagreements and refine evaluation prior to editorial decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial decision-making process
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on the arguments and recommendations of the referees, the academic editors and the executive editor decide whether to offer publication or revision, or whether to reject the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions may involve further consultation with the referees, advisory experts and/or the authors. Editors may seek an arbitrating expert when needed. Revisions are invited only for manuscripts with a high probability of acceptance after one major round of experimental revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may appeal decisions if there is concrete evidence of a misunderstanding or mistake at the editorial or referee level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals are evaluated in depth and without prejudice. Authors should supply concrete evidence of errors or misunderstandings in the original decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent peer review policy (no confidential referee comments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Life Science Alliance has no ‘Confidential Comments’ on the referee reporting forms; all comments will be transmitted to the authors and the other referees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees should be aware that all comments will be visible to authors and other referees. If confidential communication with the editor is necessary (e.g., ethical concerns, data integrity, biosecurity, or conflicts), this can be done by email to the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of editorial correspondence for accepted/ transferred manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: For accepted manuscripts that were directly submitted to Life Science Alliance or initially reviewed at EMBO Press journals or JCB and subsequently transferred with referee reports to Life Science Alliance, all formal correspondence between authors and editors relevant to the decision process, as well as the overall timeline, will be published as an online supplementary document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referee anonymity will be maintained unless the referee decides to sign the report (open peer review). Authors can opt out of the transparent process at any stage prior to publication; authors may request specific redactions (e.g., material intended for publication elsewhere) but must notify the editorial office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scooping protection from submission date
rubrics_metrics.description: Other papers published in peer‑reviewed journals or manuscripts posted on recognized preprint servers after submission of a manuscript to Life Science Alliance are not considered relevant to the editorial assessment of the submitted manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A manuscript submitted to Life Science Alliance is subject to scooping protection from the day of submission and this extends through the agreed revision period. For invited transfers, protection applies from submission to partner journals if transferred to LSA within 4 months of transfer invitation. Protection also applies from the day of posting on a recognized preprint server if submitted to LSA within 4 months of posting. Scooping protection does not apply to related papers with an overlapping set of authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation and disclosure obligations for related work
rubrics_metrics.description: Related papers and appropriate preprints must be cited if they are published before the manuscript proofs stage; related manuscripts submitted, in press or published elsewhere must be declared at submission and cited where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should inform editors as soon as they become aware of other studies directly relevant to their study. It is at the discretion of the editors whether prior publication of related material prevents subsequent publication in Life Science Alliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer policy and use of transferred referee reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Life Science Alliance accepts manuscripts rejected from journals at EMBO Press, Rockefeller University Press, and Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory Press following instructions appended to the editorial decision letter; both peer‑reviewed and non‑peer‑reviewed manuscripts can be transferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts transferred post review will automatically include the referees’ reports and identities of referees (unless the referee has opted out). Authors are invited to include a point‑by‑point rebuttal and a revised manuscript as part of the transfer. Editors will aim to use the transferred referee reports in arriving at a rapid decision and may involve an arbitrating expert; transfers from non‑partner journals are possible at the editors’ discretion if anonymous, authenticated referee reports are available. LSA also invites authors to have reviewer reports and referee identities confidentially transferred by the editor to another recognized journal to minimize futile review cycles; referees can opt out of transferring their identities.
